title: Would you use a backtester where you just describe the strategy in plain English? Trying to work out if this is a real problem or just mine.
author: ashutosh_811
selftext:
Right now, checking whether a strategy works on Indian equities means either coding it yourself (weeks of plumbing before you learn anything), using a template-driven tool that only supports the twelve strategies it already knows, or trusting a CAGR screenshot from someone with no way to verify the universe, the costs, or the fills.

I have a backtest engine running over \~8 years of NSE data — I've put seven common strategies through it and five failed, including two I was sure about. I'm considering putting a chat box in front of it: describe a strategy in a sentence, get the equity curve, the drawdown, and whether the trades were fillable at your size. Tweak it in follow-up messages instead of rewriting code.

Before I build the front end, three things I'm unsure about:

1. Do people actually want to **test** strategies, or want to be **told what to buy**? 
2. Has a backtest ever changed what you actually did — or did you trade it anyway?
3. Does plain-English input matter, or would you rather have knobs and dropdowns?

Not selling anything, no link, nothing to sign up for. And if this already exists and I've missed it, please tell me,  that'd save me months.

comments.author: TheAlxOf96
comments.body: Its 100% possible. Very important not to run the backtest via AI just let them code the file you run your backtest on. There is a guy on YouTube „tickstream backtesting“ he shares a md file which prevents the ai from a lot of mistakes. I highly recommend watching it. Md file is free no course sh\*\*.

replies.author: ashutosh_811
replies.body: Got it! But will you use it?

replies.author: TheAlxOf96
replies.body: Im using it and it fixed/killes two of my algos. For sure annoying xD but saves you from fooling yourself
